text: dsh-bottom-cost 是 DeepSeek Harness 网页端的会话费用插件，在输入框下方统计栏显示费用胶囊。它通过会话投影按轮整理模型调用的 token，再按当前价目表在浏览器计算费用。面板展示每轮花费、缓存命中与未命中金额、总额及未计价调用，并可跳转到对应轮次；用户也能手动刷新官方 DeepSeek 价目页、查看变化后选择采用。适合想核对 DeepSeek 对话 token 费用的 DSH 用户；其他 provider 显示未计价。无需 API key，刷新价目时才请求官方定价页面。

dsh-bottom-cost adds a cost chip below the composer in DSH web. It estimates per-turn CNY costs from token usage, showing cache-hit and cache-miss amounts. Users can refresh the official DeepSeek price page, review and apply changes. Other providers are unpriced; no API key is needed.
想知道这段 DSH 对话大概花了多少 token 费用。
能不能把每一轮模型调用的费用分别列出来？
我想看缓存命中和未命中分别贡献了多少费用。
让 DSH 在输入框下面显示当前会话的花费。
DeepSeek 改价后，怎么用新价格重新估算之前的对话？
我能从费用面板直接跳到产生这笔费用的对话轮次吗？
How can I see the estimated cost of each turn in my DSH conversation?
Can I refresh DeepSeek prices and recalculate what this conversation would cost?
dsh-bottom-cost 的功能「逐轮费用统计」：在输入框下方展示会话总费用和各轮费用，并拆分缓存命中与未命中部分。点击轮次标签可定位到对话中相应轮次。
dsh-bottom-cost 的功能「按时段估价」：根据调用时刻的北京时间峰谷时段、模型和 token 数，按价目表计算缓存命中、未命中输入及输出费用；非 DeepSeek 官方路由标记为未计价。
dsh-bottom-cost 的功能「刷新并采用价目」：用户从面板触发刷新，插件抓取并解析 DeepSeek 官方中文定价页，展示候选价目与变化；用户选择采用后，价目保存到 DSH 家目录并用于重算费用。
dsh-bottom-cost 的功能「会话历史回填」：通过 DSH session projection 汇总会话事件，晚注册或宿主重启后可从内存事件日志回放已发生轮次；明细最多保留最近 200 轮。
dsh-bottom-cost 按 token 和公开价目估算费用，不读取账户余额或实际扣款；没有公开价目的其他 provider 调用会标为未计价。
dsh-bottom-cost 仅在用户触发刷新时请求 api-docs.deepseek.com；采用的价目表写入 DSH 家目录的 dsh-bottom-cost/pricebook.json。

dsh-bottom-cost README · dsh-bottom-cost：[English](README.md) | [中文](README.zh.md)

A **session cost** chip for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): it sits in the same row as the built-in stats pills under the composer and answers "what has this conversation cost" and "what did the last turn cost" at a glance, splitting the spend into **cache-hit** and **cache-miss** parts.

text:
dsh-bottom-cost README · Option 1 — install it from the DSH UI (simplest)：The host half is a Node module, so **a config reload alone will not import it** — that restart is not optional. Once restarted, open the UI and the chip is there; no page refresh needed.

**Updating later is explicit.** An installation pins the exact version (the profile ends up with `"dsh-bottom-cost": "0.5.1"`), so a new release reaches you when you press **更新** (Update) in the plugin manager — nothing changes under you in between.

dsh-bottom-cost README · Option 4 — from source (developers)：For hacking on it, or for a non-default profile:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/LanFeng97/dsh-bottom-cost
cd dsh-bottom-cost
node tools/install.mjs              # copy into the profile's node_modules + append one loader line
node tools/install.mjs --dry-run    # print what it would do, write nothing

dsh-bottom-cost README · Option 4 — from source (developers)：It is idempotent — re-run it after a `git pull` to sync an update — and it resolves your DSH home the way the harness does (`$DSH_HOME`, then `~/.dsh`). This route needs a restart too. After that, changing `lib/client.js` only needs a page refresh; changing `lib/index.js` still needs a restart.

dsh-bottom-cost README · Option 4 — from source (developers)：The plugin has **no runtime dependencies at all** (its shape validation is a ~90-line file it ships, `lib/shape.js`), so this route installs nothing from the network. That is also why it installs by **copy** rather than a directory junction: a junction gets realpath-resolved back into the clone, so any future bare import of a third-party package would fail to resolve there at load time.

dsh-bottom-cost README · Cannot install or cannot uninstall? Read this first：**The desktop client can only install npm sources.** On the official desktop app, pasting a GitHub URL into "add plugin" may simply not install — that is the client's install boundary, not your network (its own message says so: "This desktop client can only install plugins published to npm"). Install by npm package name instead.
section: Cannot install or cannot uninstall? Read this first

text: dsh-bottom-cost README · Cannot install or cannot uninstall? Read this first：**A flaky network breaks the GitHub source.** Behind that box is pnpm: it resolves `owner/repo` to a commit, then downloads a tarball from `codeload.github.com`, and the resolve step has a **6-second timeout**. A hiccup fails the install; retrying usually gets through.
section: Cannot install or cannot uninstall? Read this first

text:
dsh-bottom-cost README · Cannot install or cannot uninstall? Read this first：**Do not mix the two install routes (important).** Once you installed through the plugin manager / market, **do not also run `tools/install.mjs`** (and do not have an AI run it) — and vice versa. The script appends its own loader row to the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`, while the plugin manager declares the same component too. With the same component declared in **two layers**, the manager refuses to disable or uninstall it:

> 卸载失败：其他配置仍在使用这个组合包的组件，请先停用它们
section: Cannot install or cannot uninstall? Read this first

dsh-bottom-cost README · Cannot install or cannot uninstall? Read this first：(An uninstall failed: another configuration still uses this bundle's components — disable those first.)

Its "disable" toggle cannot suppress the other layer either, which is why a **disabled plugin keeps working and survives a restart**.

**What to do** (in order):

1. Open `<DSH install dir>/dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml` and **delete this whole block** (comment line plus the three `insert` lines):

text: dsh-bottom-cost README · How to read the UI：In the screenshot: the bottom line is the **stats row under the composer** — `◎ ¥5.294 · ¥0.9230` is this plugin, sitting in the same row as the built-in `15 轮 388 步 · 228 tok/s` (session stats) and `147M tok · 缓存命中 99%` (token usage) pills, with the context meter at the far right. Above it is the **expanded panel**.

dsh-bottom-cost README · How to read the UI：Clicking a **Turn N** heading jumps the conversation to that turn: it read-only drives the built-in turn rail on the right, so a turn that is not loaded yet gets paged in by the app itself before landing. When it cannot locate the turn, the panel says so at the bottom instead of failing silently.

dsh-bottom-cost README · How to read the UI：Each turn also shows **which model it used**, right of the turn number (`v4-pro`, `v4-flash`, …; only the `deepseek-` prefix is trimmed, a turn that mixed models lists them side by side, and hovering reveals the full ids).

dsh-bottom-cost README · How to read the UI：The **sun (or moon)** at the right of the title row is a light/dark switch that applies **to this plugin's content only**: both the panel and the cost chip in the stats row flip to the other palette, and the app's global theme is untouched. The icon shows the current mode (sun = light, moon = dark), and the colours come from the two official theme definitions — so each mode matches the rest of DSH while being the opposite of it. When the chip is on the opposite theme it gets its own themed background, since near-white text on the light stats row would otherwise be unreadable.

dsh-bottom-cost README · How to read the UI：**The chip in the stats row**

```
◎ ¥2.922 · ¥0.4877
  ↑ left                ↑ right
this conversation's     the latest turn's
total spend             spend

- The **left** number is what this conversation has cost so far; the **right** number is what the most recent turn cost. Both update live as the conversation goes on.
- With nothing billable yet, the chip is hidden — the same "no content, no render" behaviour as the built-in stats pills.

**Click the chip and the panel opens upward**

dsh-bottom-cost README · How to read the UI：- **Fixed header**: the conversation's total spend, split into **cache-hit** and **cache-miss** (`¥1.609` and `¥1.313` in the screenshot). Those two always add up to the total on the chip — the identity `total = hit + miss` holds by construction, not by rounding luck.
- **Scrolling list**: **every turn's** spend, three rows each — **total / cache-hit / cache-miss** (turns 7 and 8 in the screenshot). It starts at the newest turn; **scroll up** to walk back through earlier ones.
- **The scrolling window is exactly two turn blocks tall** — you came here to see this turn and the previous one, and the panel does not have to grow tall for that.

dsh-bottom-cost README · How to read the UI：It is about the **price list used for pricing**, not about re-counting your conversation. Clicking it makes the host fetch the **official Chinese price page**, parse its 12 unit prices and validate every one, then **show you the diff first** (which line changed, from what to what) — nothing is applied until you click **采用 (Apply)**. That extra step exists because DeepSeek publishes **no machine-readable price API**, only a human-facing docs page, so parsing it can fail; a bad parse applied silently would corrupt every number you look at.

dsh-bottom-cost README · How to read the UI：The panel's second line — `价目：官方页 · 10/13 02:17` — tells you **which price list is active and when it was fetched**. If it says `价目：内置表`, no fetch has happened yet and the built-in table shipped with the plugin is in use.

dsh-bottom-cost README · How to read the UI：**Do you need to click it often?** No. Once when the official prices change. After you apply, **the whole conversation is instantly re-priced** (money is computed in the browser from the active price list; history stores only token facts), so you never end up with two generations of prices mixed into one ledger.
dsh-bottom-cost README · Where the numbers come from：Only the **official DeepSeek routes** have a published price list, so only they produce money:

dsh-bottom-cost README · Where the numbers come from：| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Hit spend** | cache-read tokens × hit price |
| **Miss spend** | (uncached input + cache-write) × miss price **+** output tokens × output price |
| **Peak / off-peak** | Beijing time Mon–Fri 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–18:00 are peak (double price); weekends and Chinese public holidays are off-peak all day |
| **When it is priced** | At the instant each call happened, taken from the session event's own timestamp — so replaying months-old history is priced with the tariff of *that* moment, not today's |
| **Other providers** | Never guessed at ¥0: they show as *unpriced*, and the panel reports how many calls were unpriced |

dsh-bottom-cost README · Where the numbers come from：Scope is the **current conversation's own turns**. A subagent is a different session and is deliberately not folded in, so the chip's numbers line up one-to-one with the turns you can see.

dsh-bottom-cost README · It is an estimate, not a bill：Prices are estimated from token counts and the published tariff. The plugin never reads your balance, never touches credentials, and cannot see what DeepSeek actually deducted.
section: It is an estimate, not a bill

So 0.5.1 **removed the fence**: a `deepseek-v4-pro` request is always priced on its own row (miss 4.5/9.0, output 13.5/27.0), and the `按Flash档估` mark plus its summary line are gone too, since their premise no longer holds.

text:
dsh-bottom-cost README · The full price-refresh flow：1. The host fetches the **official Chinese price page** (`api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/quick_start/pricing`, which quotes CNY; the English page quotes USD and is not used).
2. It parses the table and validates all 12 unit prices — if any single one is missing or implausible, the whole parse is rejected.
3. It shows you **the diff**; **采用 (Apply)** commits it, **放弃 (Discard)** throws it away.

dsh-bottom-cost README · The full price-refresh flow：The price list is stored in `<DSH_HOME>/dsh-bottom-cost/pricebook.json` (atomic write) and survives restarts. A failed fetch (offline, timeout, redesigned page) is reported and **keeps the current prices**; the built-in table remains the first-run fallback.

dsh-bottom-cost README · Capability boundary：- **One outbound request**, to the public docs page above, **only when you click 刷新**. Nothing else ever leaves the machine.
- **One file written**: `<DSH_HOME>/dsh-bottom-cost/pricebook.json`.
- The three price routes are **loopback + same-origin fenced** (the same guard sibling DSH plugins use).
- The host half reads no credentials, writes no session data, and runs no timers.
- The **Turn N** headings read-only drive the built-in turn navigation: they read the tick buttons' `aria-label` (which carries the turn number) and `aria-current`, and invoke the tick's own click. If the rail is unavailable it falls back to the `data-chat-turn` anchors on transcript rows. The plugin injects no nodes, changes no layout, and hardcodes no build-hashed class names — but if those semantic attributes ever change, jumping breaks and the panel reports the failure instead of failing silently.

dsh-bottom-cost README · Why the shape validation is hand-rolled：DSH's projection registry asks each unit for a `stateSchema` and a `wire.viewSchema`, and **only ever calls `.parse` on them** (six call sites in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-projection`; no `safeParse`, no `optional`, no `refine`). That contract is duck-typed, so `lib/shape.js` implements exactly the seven predicates this plugin needs — object, string, finite number, boolean, array, enum, nullable — in about 90 dependency-free lines.
section: Why the shape validation is hand-rolled

text: dsh-bottom-cost README · Why the shape validation is hand-rolled：The alternative was `zod`, as DSH's own `dsh-token-meter` uses. It is not wrong, but for this plugin it loses: the published package is 840 files / 5.86 MB (even a trimmed v4-ESM subset is 111 files / 886 KB), and the README's primary install path is a *copy* install that does not bring dependencies along — so shipping zod would mean either a large vendored blob, or a pnpm/network step that rewrites your profile's `package.json`. Hand-rolling keeps that path genuinely self-contained. It is slightly *stricter* than zod in one place: `NaN` and `Infinity` are rejected (they would silently poison a running total), and it is covered by the self-test suite directly — which zod, being a third-party import, could not be.
section: Why the shape validation is hand-rolled

text:
dsh-bottom-cost README · Official extension points, not DOM injection：- The chip registers into the built-in slot **`conversation.composer.dock`** (`order: 1`; the shipped `stats` pills take `order: 0`). That slot *is* the stats row under the composer, a `display:flex; gap:12px` row, so the chip is a first-class sibling of the built-in pills — no DOM poking, no fight with re-renders.
- The panel reuses `useAnchoredPosition` and `useDismissOnOutsidePointer` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives`, the same pair the built-in stats dialogs use, so placement, clamping, outside-click and Esc behave identically.
- All styling goes through theme CSS variables (`--dsw-*`), so it follows your theme instead of hard-coding colors.
section: Official extension points, not DOM injection

text: dsh-bottom-cost README · Token facts travel as a session projection：The host registers a **session projection unit** (`sessionCost`) and the browser reads it with `useProjection('sessionCost')`. That buys three things for free:
section: Token facts travel as a session projection

text:
dsh-bottom-cost README · Token facts travel as a session projection：- **History backfill.** The projection registry replays a late-registered unit over the in-memory log on first touch, so after installing or restarting DSH the turns that *already happened* in the current conversation are folded in — the chip does not start at ¥0.
- **Persistence.** State rides the harness's projection checkpoint cache, so the plugin writes no data files of its own.
- **Push, not polling.** Values arrive on the session control stream; there is no timer and no fetch loop.
section: Token facts travel as a session projection

text:
dsh-bottom-cost README · Layered so it can be tested without DSH：| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `lib/fold.js` | Pure fold: session events → per-turn token facts. Zero dependencies. |
| `lib/pricing.js` | Pure pricing: peak/off-peak clock, model→price-row decision, tokens→money. Zero dependencies. |
| `lib/pricebook.js` | Pure price book: built-in table, strict validation, official-page parser. Zero dependencies. |
| `lib/projection.js` | Thin adapter: the shape schemas + the client view. |
| `lib/pricebook-store.js` | Fetch, stage a candidate, apply, persist. |
| `lib/routes.js`, `lib/guard.js` | Loopback-fenced HTTP translation. |
| `lib/client.js` | The chip and the panel; computes money from facts × the active book. |
section: Layered so it can be tested without DSH

text:
dsh-bottom-cost README · Tests：```sh
npm test              # node tools/selftest.mjs — 66 checks, no network
npm run test:live     # node tools/live-check.mjs — fetch the real page, parse, persist, read back
npm run test:schema   # node tools/schema-check.mjs — schema ↔ state ↔ view consistency, from the installed copy
```

dsh-bottom-cost README · Tests：`selftest` covers peak/off-peak and holiday exceptions, the parser (against a checked-in snapshot of the official page), price-book validation, re-pricing under a different book, per-bucket aggregation, replay idempotence, JSON-safe state, list trimming, the client's i18n key set, and — since the validators are now the plugin's own code — the projection schemas themselves (unknown fields stripped, wrong types rejected with a path, `NaN` refused).

dsh-bottom-cost README · Tests：`test:schema` is a different kind of check: it imports the copy that is **actually installed in the profile** and drives state → view → schema through it, so it catches both "the installed files can load" and "`viewOf()` and the view schema still agree field-for-field". That second seam broke once in development; it has its own guard now.

dsh-bottom-cost README · Compatibility：- DSH **≥ 0.2.0-rc.2** (built and verified against 0.2.0-rc.2).
- Node **≥ 20**.
- **No runtime dependencies.** The projection schemas are validated by the plugin's own `lib/shape.js`.

The flip side: when the official prices change, the two **copies** each need updating (that is what "same tariff interpretation" is warning about).

dsh-bottom-cost README · No runtime coupling：**Zero runtime dependencies.** Nothing to install alongside, nothing to keep in sync: the projection schemas come from the plugin's own `lib/shape.js` (see "Why the shape validation is hand-rolled" above).
